parsed.explanation: Combined regime exposes a trans visitor to broad entry denial/deportation for perceived queerness without charge or conviction, documented app entrapment especially of trans women, morality/sex-work prosecutions carrying prison, blackmail, custody abuse and coerced anal examinations, with no anti-discrimination recourse and pervasive healthcare discrimination. Hostile state framing and 2017 mass arrests show organised targeting. Severity is severe, though no death penalty or current forced-examination case is documented, keeping it above the 0.05 tier.

entry_documents.exposure: Interior ministry may deny entry or deport anyone deemed to disturb public order/morality; 12 incidents 2018-2022 applied this to travellers perceived as queer, without upheld charges.
entry_documents.interaction: Perception at entry can trigger removal, and any later police encounter can also lead to deportation rather than prosecution.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented entrapment via dating apps, blackmail, arrests, physical abuse and coerced anal examinations in custody; 84 arrests after September 2017 flag incident.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: App contact can become arrest, custody abuse, or deportation; complaints are documented as ignored.

federal_state_facilities.interaction: No documented bathroom, ward or custody-placement rule; absence is not safety given documented custody abuse.

care_services.exposure: Pervasive gender-identity/sexual-orientation discrimination in healthcare and barriers to equitable services documented in 2025 human-rights review submission.
care_services.interaction: Emergency or routine care could involve outing and discriminatory treatment, with no anti-discrimination remedy.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Vague morality/debauchery and 1961 sex-work provisions, read without financial-exchange requirement, support arrests and prison sentences; officials incite and media outing fed 2017 arrests.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State threat-framing increases police discretion at borders, in public, and on dating apps.

minors_guardians.interaction: No age-specific rule documented; a minor travelling with a guardian would face the same combined entry, police and care exposures as an adult.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Police are documented perpetrators through entrapment, blackmail, arrests and custody abuse; authorities turn a blind eye to coerced examinations.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Seeking police help risks outing, arrest or deportation rather than protection.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No statutory anti-discrimination protection; legal gender recognition loophole was closed nationwide in 2024, a climate signal of institutional hostility.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Resident recognition closure does not itself govern a visitor's passport, but no documented remedy offsets active entry, policing and detention exposures.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in recurring state targeting, imprisonment and custody abuse with failed recourse; lower than 0.15-A only because no explicit presentation offence, mandatory sweeps or documented men's-facility sexual assault pattern is shown for trans visitors.

More severe than 0.25-A: adds broad deportation without conviction, prison-carrying morality prosecutions, coerced anal examinations and a 2017 mass-arrest wave, not only short detention and extortion.

Materially below 0.35-C: police extortion there usually ends in release after payment, whereas here documented outcomes include imprisonment, forced examinations, custody abuse and removal without charge.

parsed.synthesis: The operative interaction is discovery-to-state-action: border discretion, app entrapment or public visibility can lead to questioning, blackmail, arrest under morality/sex-work law, abusive custody or deportation, with no effective complaint route. Nationwide administrative uniformity removes regional mitigation. The absence of sourced trans-specific entry screening, facility rules, homicide rates and post-2017 forced-examination cases limits certainty, but documented 2018-2022 deportations and 2026 routine-use reporting establish a current, organised exposure well below the 0.25 anchor.
